added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own baseline_suite/after_suite: target-base.log (cb2791806) and target-head.log (372ef575b) both record 0 failures at EXIT=0, so no id was added; the 2 failures in head-part_00.log sit on a separate wider arm the manifest names and attributes to xdist parallel load.

findings.text: blocking: the sweep is wired only into `watch`, which `reckon crew watch` reaches only with --once/--exit-on-empty (reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:3267); the fleet's default following producer is watch_ticker (reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:2238, reached at reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:3236), so §37's deliverable -- the sweep that resumes an unfollowed session's lapsed hold and reviews its finished run -- does not take effect in production.

follow-on: the call `with suppress(CrewError): sweep_unfollowed_sessions(project)` inside watch() is guarded by no assertion; the test calls sweep_unfollowed_sessions() directly, so deleting the wiring at reckon/crew/runs.py:3262-3263 reddens no test.

follow-on: `assert WATCHER_SWEEP_GRACE_SECONDS == 600.0` compares the module constant against a literal restating it, so the two sides move together and it can fail only if the constant is edited; the grace boundary is already asserted by the eleven/nine-minute arms at lines 150-155.
follow-on: the test drives sweep_unfollowed_sessions() directly rather than the watcher's tick the done_when names, so it proves the helper and not its wiring into any loop.

follow-on: a session with no follower registration at all (follower_lock_path absent) yields None from _follower_last_seen_seconds and is therefore swept with no grace at all, diverging from the plan's ten-minute window and untested by the three-session fixture.

follow-on: the reviewed worktree carries an uncommitted change wiring runs.sweep_unfollowed_sessions into watch_ticker, outside the node's two commits and its covered paths; it is a peer's in-flight work, recorded so its presence is not mistaken for the node's landing.
